text: Git branching is a powerful feature that helps teams manage changes to their code without disrupting the main project. In a typical version control workflow, developers create feature branches to work on new ideas or fixes independently. Once the work is complete, they merge it back into the main branch, often through a pull request. This process allows for code review and discussion before integrating the changes. Using branches keeps the main code stable while multiple people contribute simultaneously. It also makes it easy to track changes, revert mistakes, and collaborate efficiently. Understanding branches is essential for any modern software team.
